findings.text: this branch is shared with the CLI, so from the moment this lands the CLI resolves pause/resume/width to /work/projects/imas_gpu/agents/control/router-gate.json (ABSENT) while the live router (job 1277263, started before this change) still publishes config_path /home/ITER/mcintos/public/imas-ambix/router-gate.json (read from the live lane document at 2026-09-25T23:25Z, width 14): a control write issued between this landing and the lead-authorised copy-and-restart writes the new file, reports success, and the live router never reads it - a silent no-effect - and the landing record's "What was not done" paragraph names the deploy step but not this interim window, so a reader of the record alone could issue such a write believing it took.

the write path creates the parent with mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) and writes a scratch then replaces it, so a control write made before the deploy creates the group directory with the process umask (0022 here, giving 0755) rather than the 2775 the section intends - after which later group members cannot write that directory and their control writes fail until chmod - and each write replaces the file with a 0644 inode, so the 664 file mode is not preserved by subsequent writes and group-write access in practice depends on the directory's write bit, which the deploy must set before the first CLI write.

the resolution-order statements outside this node's declared scope are now stale: this docstring still enumerates the order as the command-line path, AMBIX_ROUTER_GATE_PATH, then the lane document's sibling with no site step, the comment at cli.py:3294 still says the lane document branch always resolves, the --gate-file help strings at cli.py:1735, :3406, :3463 and :3493 still say the option overrides AMBIX_ROUTER_GATE_PATH and the lane document's sibling, and imas_ambix/agent/slurm.py:985 still says a job submitted without the option keeps reading the lane document's sibling - which the new default falsifies, since such a job now reads the group control path - so the reconciliation is a follow-on on those two files.

these two assertions pinning the sibling fallback (with the docstring at :125, 'An existing deployment that names nothing keeps today's behaviour') now hold only because the new fixture blanks the site value, and the contract they state is one production no longer follows: a deployment that names nothing now reads the site control path, so the assertion pair and its docstring need reconciling with the default by the file's owner rather than being left as the description of current behaviour.

the record says 'Seven tests added in tests/test_agent_gate_site_default.py' and then enumerates eight distinct things, and the file defines eight (tests/test_agent_gate_site_default.py:49 through :138); the same miscount appears in the run's manifest, so a reader counting the tests finds a discrepancy in the two artifacts that carry the count.

the new module's docstring keeps the change's chronology - 'used to be inferred from the lane document, so control lived beside the published lane in a personal public directory' - where the naming rule for a test asks for the invariant and the failure mode rather than the history (the same check that bans 'used to be' prose in code), and the sentence reads at least as strongly rewritten as 'the lane document's sibling sits in a personal public directory shared with observations and a large request log, so the control file defaults to the group-owned control directory'.
